title: Preserve structured schema and bind tool-handshake for Responses v2 compatibility
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customers building deterministic, schema-driven pipelines reported incompatibilities when using the new Responses v2 variants through our OpenAI-compat adapter: structured_output schemas were being flattened in the proxy, and tool/function call handshakes sometimes lost the deterministic seed and metadata headers during streaming reassembly. This PR ensures structured_output schemas are preserved end-to-end and introduces an explicit tool-handshake binding so tool calls keep deterministic flags and metadata passthrough throughout streaming. Summary of changes and checklist: - Add schema-preserve pass in the OpenAI adapter to map Responses.v2 structured_output -> internal structured token framing without losing field-level annotations. - Implement an idempotent tool-handshake binding between the adapter and runtime so tool/function calls are associated with the same request seed and metadata across retries and reconnects. - Improve streaming frame reassembly to tolerate partial toolcall frames and avoid dropping trailing annotations (fixes regression where last frame lost rng/determinism hints). - Add deterministic-seed propagation in transport headers and ensure the seed is embedded in the framing for replay and offline eval. - Add e2e smoke tests and integration fixtures for tool-binding across reconnects, and a deterministic-seed test harness for CI. - Update Python SDK client behavior to forward structured_output schema and deterministic options when using the OpenAI compat layer. - Documentation: compatibility notes and migration steps (docs/compat/responses-v2.md). Checklist: [x] unit tests updated [x] integration tests added [x] e2e smoke runs green [x] changelog entry [x] rollout plan included Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag (resp_v2_schema_preserve). Start with internal canary, then gated beta for customers with explicit toggles, fallback to strict-openai-compat if issues observed. Backwards compatibility: adapter defaults are no-op until the feature flag is set. This change preserves OpenAI-contracted behavior unless the customer opts-in to the new schema-preserve mode. Breaking change: none expected; feature gate ensures safe rollout. CI: small flakiness observed in e2e tool-binding test on first run; re-ran with increased timeouts and it stabilized. See CI summary below. Detailed commit summary, files changed and review notes are included as separate fields in this PR JSON for traceability.

release_notes: Preserve structured_output schemas through the OpenAI-compat adapter and introduce an idempotent tool-handshake binding that keeps deterministic seeds and metadata intact during streaming and reconnects. Rollout behind feature flag 'resp_v2_schema_preserve'.

notes_on_testing: Unit tests: adapter mapping (+), framer (+), handshake idempotency (+). Integration: tool-binding reconnect scenarios (stable after timeout increase). E2E: deterministic-seed smoke tests run in CI canary with feature flag on; first run flaky, second run passed. Load tests: micro-bench shows <3% overhead when schema_preserve pass is enabled for typical short-chat workloads.
post_merge_actions: Feature flag will be initially enabled only for internal canary cluster and a small beta cohort. Monitor telemetry: schema-preserve failure rate, handshake retry counts, stream-reassembly error rate. If regressions observed, flip feature flag to disable and roll back the compat pass. Update SDKs with explicit opt-in examples in next patch release.
migration_guide: For customers using OpenAI-compat and Responses v2: - To opt-in, set 'resp_v2_schema_preserve=true' at the route config or runtime feature flags. - SDKs (Python) will forward structured_output and deterministic options automatically when feature is enabled. - If your tooling depends on legacy flattened fields, do not enable until you confirm downstream consumers accept the structured format. - For tool integrations, ensure your tool handshake satisfies the new idempotency semantics (stateless resume supported).
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the adapter change behind a feature flag to reduce blast radius. The design preserves compatibility with existing OpenAI-contracted flows unless explicitly enabled.
